categories.name: Clarifying questions
categories.feedback: Asked nothing about the bank's goal, data and labels, latency, or the cost of a missed fraud versus a false alarm.

categories.name: Problem framing
categories.feedback: A 70% fraud-probability threshold implies a probability target, but no inputs, no baseline, and no plan for building a first model.

categories.name: Metrics & evaluation
categories.feedback: Noted the 0.1% imbalance but named no metric, validation split or failure modes; the 70% cutoff was unjustified.

categories.name: Communication
categories.feedback: Clear but very short; mostly restated the question with no structure or trade-offs.

summary: Say how you'd evaluate and set the threshold: accuracy is useless at 0.1% fraud, so name precision/recall or PR-AUC and pick the threshold from the cost of a missed fraud versus a false alarm.

categories.name: Clarifying questions
categories.feedback: Said the cause was identified but not how; nothing about asking about targets, data or constraints.

categories.name: Problem framing
categories.feedback: Clear arc: missed targets, no CI/CD tests as root cause, evaluation tests in CI, regression tests in CD; 'missed targets' left vague.

categories.name: Metrics & evaluation
categories.feedback: Mentioned regression tests, 90% of targets and no drift, but named no metric, validation approach or drift monitoring.

categories.name: Communication
categories.feedback: Concise and logically ordered; 'Closed CD' unclear and no trade-offs or stakeholder impact.

summary: Name the metric and numbers: which metric missed target and by how much, what the evaluation tests checked, and how drift was measured.
